## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Peru ERM 2026: regions where the leading gubernatorial ticket is below 30% of valid votes (research notes as of Oct 5, 2026)

Note: the resolution snapshot is Oct 15, 2026 at 23:59 Peru time. Everything below is from Oct 4–5, before the snapshot. It is context only and does not resolve the question.

## 1. Resolution source

**ONPE portal:**
- https://resultados.onpe.gob.pe/ returned HTTP 403 when fetched on Oct 5, 2026.
- The alternate URL RPP links to, https://resultadoelectoral.onpe.gob.pe/main/resumen, returned a 302 redirect that was not followed.
- **We could not read ONPE directly.** All the ONPE figures below come second-hand from news outlets.

**Metaculus FAQ** (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) also returned 403 on Oct 5, so its definition of credible sources is not quoted here.

**The 30% rule:** Ley 27683 art. 5, as amended by Ley 30305, says a ticket needs at least 30% of valid votes to win in the first round. Otherwise the top two go to a runoff, which the JNE has kept on **Nov 29, 2026**. ONPE asked to move it to Dec 6 and the JNE declined (Infobae, Oct 5, 14:25: https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/10/05/segunda-vuelta-en-las-elecciones-regionales-cuando-se-realiza/).

**ONPE cómputo by region.** Main source is Infobae's live ONPE table, cut at about 08:26 on Oct 5 (https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/10/04/resultados-onpe-en-vivo-las-cifras-oficiales-de-las-regiones-de-las-elecciones-de-hoy-4-de-octubre-de-2026/). Later updates from RPP, El Comercio and La República are in brackets. The figures were read through a summarising fetch tool, so the decimals could have small errors.

**Implied ONPE-based count as of the afternoon of Oct 5: 14 regions below 30%.** This is our own tally of reported ONPE figures. No outlet has published an ONPE-based list.

**Regions closest to the line:**
- Junín is under by 0.76 points at 96.9% of actas.
- Ica is over by 0.77 points at about 98%.
- Cusco, San Martín and Huánuco are about 1.1–1.8 points over, at 88–93% of actas.
- Huancavelica and Ucayali: the ONPE figures conflict with the exit poll, and the Huancavelica numbers were also inconsistent between sources.
- Loreto had the least of its actas counted.

## 2. News, status quo and schedule

**Media counts that are not ONPE's cómputo.** These would not count for resolution:
- **Trome, Oct 4:** Datum exit poll, 15 runoffs.
- **La República, Oct 5:** 14, https://larepublica.pe/politica/2026/10/05/si-habra-segunda-vuelta-en-las-elecciones-regionales-2026-las-14-regiones-que-irian-a-las-urnas-en-noviembre-295210
- **Infobae and Gestión, Oct 5:** 14, also Datum. Datum's 14 include Huancavelica, Ica and Ucayali, and leave out Junín, Pasco and Tacna.
- **El Comercio, Oct 5, "20 de 25":** https://elcomercio.pe/elecciones/lima/elecciones-2026-20-de-25-regiones-iran-a-segunda-vuelta-segun-boca-de-urna-de-datum-apuesplan-ultimas-noticia/
- **El Comercio map, Oct 5, 13 regions:** Amazonas, Áncash, Arequipa, Huancavelica, Ica, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Lima, Loreto, Moquegua, Piura, Puno, Tumbes. https://elcomercio.pe/lima/sucesos/el-nuevo-mapa-del-peru-tras-las-elecciones-las-13-regiones-donde-habra-segunda-vuelta-y-los-candidatos-que-iran-al-balotaje-apuesplan-noticia/ . It seems to mix in exit-poll data: it includes Huancavelica and Ica, and leaves out Junín, Pasco and Tacna, which are under 30% in ONPE's count. Uncertain.

**ONPE progress:**
- ONPE began publishing at 17:00 on Oct 4 (El Peruano).
- By Oct 5, Lima Metropolitana and five unnamed regions were at 100% of actas *processed* (El Comercio). In Lima Metropolitana about 7.3% of actas were flagged ("observadas") and sent to the local electoral courts (JEE).
- Per-region counted share on Oct 5 ranged from about 56% (Loreto) to about 99%.

**Scheduled events:**
- **Oct 11:** deadline for ONPE to send flagged regional actas to the JEEs. This is the only dated milestone before the snapshot.
- **Oct 28:** deadline for the JEEs to resolve those actas and hold recounts.
- Source: Gestión, Oct 4, https://gestion.pe/peru/politica/erm-2026-jne-fija-la-fecha-de-la-segunda-vuelta-de-elecciones-regionales-cuando-sera-noticia/
- Interim ONPE head Pachas said winners would be known in about 20 days; the JNE said about a month (Expreso, could not open the page).
- So the count probably **will not be fully at 100% by Oct 15**. The share counted will be high, but flagged actas in each region could still be pending.

**Disruptions that could produce flagged or annulled actas:**
- Loreto (Santa Cruz, Alto Amazonas): shots fired and ballot boxes burned (Infobae, Oct 5).
- Cajamarca (Sorochuco): voting suspended at one site after a fire from an apparent incendiary device (La República, Oct 5).
- Áncash: clashes over alleged bused-in voters (Infobae, Oct 4).

**Fragmentation:** 16 tickets in Piura, 15 in Arequipa, 9 in Puno, 8 in La Libertad.

**Prediction markets:** none found.

## 3. Base rates: regions with no ticket at 30%

| Year | Regions | Notes |

| 2010 | Unverified, about 11–12? | Sources conflict |
| 2014 | **14** | Huánuco's leader finished at 29.96%. An early NODAL list (Oct 2014) didn't include Huánuco, so it may have dropped below 30% late in the count. This is inferred, not verified. Sources: Wikipedia, América TV |
| 2018 | **15** | Andina, https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-elecciones-2018-15-regiones-habra-segunda-vuelta-para-elegir-gobernador-728840.aspx |
| 2022 | **9** | Amazonas, Cajamarca, Callao, Cusco, Lambayeque, Lima, Moquegua, Pasco, Piura. Sources: Infobae Oct 4, 2022; RPP |

**How shares drift during the count:**
- Tacna 2022: the leader fell from 32.13% at 12% of actas to 30.64% at 96.7%, and stayed above 30%.
- In general, late-counted actas move shares by about 0.5–2 points.
- In 2022 (election Oct 2), about 98% of actas were counted by Oct 10. On Oct 21 a few regions still had about 1–2% of governor actas pending at the JEEs (RPP).

## Main uncertainties
- No direct read of the ONPE portal was possible.
- The decimals come from second-hand automated reads.
- Close cases: Junín, Ica, Cusco, San Martín, Huánuco, and the conflicting Huancavelica figures.
- Loreto had the lowest share of actas counted.

criterios: This question resolves as the number of Peru's 25 regional constituencies (the 24 departments plus the Constitutional Province of Callao) in which, according to the National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE) official vote computation (cómputo oficial) for the October 4, 2026 regional gubernatorial election (Elecciones Regionales 2026), no gubernatorial-vicegubernatorial formula has obtained at least 30% of valid votes — read from ONPE's official results portal (https://resultados.onpe.gob.pe/) using the last figures displayed at or before 23:59 Peru time (UTC−5) on October 15, 2026. A region counts if the leading formula's share of valid votes is below 30.00% in the computation displayed at that time. For example, if 11 of the 25 regions show a leading formula below 30% of valid votes, this resolves as 11.
letra_pequena: The determining figure is the percentage of valid votes (votos válidos) obtained by the most-voted gubernatorial formula in each region, as shown in ONPE's official computation (not the quick count / conteo rápido) at the stated snapshot time, regardless of the share of actas (tally sheets) processed at that point. If ONPE's results portal is inaccessible or does not display the figures at the snapshot time, the count will be determined from figures reported by the Jurado Nacional de Elecciones' official platform or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reflecting ONPE's official computation as of that time. Whether a region ultimately holds the November 29, 2026 runoff (Segunda Elección Regional) after resolution of observed ballots and proclamations does not affect resolution; only the 30% threshold in the official computation as of the snapshot matters.

(b) **If nothing changed:** 14 regions, based on the reported ONPE figures from October 5.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Approximately 14–15 regions. Most counts are already advanced, but a few leaders remain close to 30%.

(d) **Experts and markets:** Historical runoff counts have ranged from 9 to 15 regions. Early media estimates cluster around 13–15, though some use exit polls rather than ONPE’s official computation. No reliable prediction-market estimate was found.

(e) **Unexpected low outcome:** Late-counted votes lift leaders in several currently sub-30% regions above the threshold.

(f) **Unexpected high outcome:** Leaders in several close, currently above-30% regions fall below it as more actas are counted.

(a) **Time left:** about 10 days, until the ONPE snapshot at 23:59 on October 15, 2026. Most regions were already at 86–99% of actas counted on October 5, so the remaining movement should be small.

(b) **If nothing changed:** 14 regions. This is the tally of reported ONPE figures as of the afternoon of October 5:
- Amazonas, Áncash, Arequipa, Junín, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Lima Provincias
- Loreto, Moquegua, Pasco, Piura, Puno, Tacna, Tumbes

(c) **If the current trend continued:** still about 14.
- Junín (29.24% at 96.9% of actas) is drifting down, so it likely stays below 30%.
- Ica (30.77% at about 98%) is reportedly safe above 30%.
- Cusco, San Martín and Huánuco are 1.1–1.8 points over with 7–12% of actas left. Each has roughly a 10–20% chance of slipping under.
- Huancavelica's figures conflict between sources (34.09% vs 31.14%, at about 81% of actas), which adds some upside risk.
- Loreto (about 28.5% at partial count) could climb over 30%, which is a small downside risk.
- On balance the expected value is slightly above 14.

(d) **Experts and markets:**
- Media counts based on the Datum exit poll mostly said 14, with outliers at 13, 15 and 20.
- The JNE's historical range is 9–15 regions.
- Past results were 14 in 2014, 15 in 2018 and 9 in 2022.
- No prediction markets were found.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** the second-hand decimals are wrong, or late rural actas push several leaders back above 30%. For example, Loreto, Tacna and Lambayeque could each recover. That would give 11–12.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** Cusco, San Martín, Huánuco and Huancavelica all slide below 30% as the remaining actas come in, or annulled actas reshuffle shares. That would give 16–18.
